 Hello,
 As of October 1, 2026, Austria’s Parcel Tax Act (Paketsteuergesetz, PakStG) is in effect. As previously communicated, the law introduces a €2.00 flat tax per order on all Business-to-Consumer (B2C) orders delivered to customers in Austria.
 The tax is mandated under Austrian law, and applies to both Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA) and Fulfilment by Merchant (FBM) orders from our France, Germany, Italy, Spain, or United Kingdom stores.
 No action is required from you. We’ll pay the tax to the Austrian Tax Authority.
 How the tax is charged
 The tax is charged once per order at checkout, regardless of the number of items in the order, or number of packages the order arrives in. The total amount is €2.40 per order (€2.00 tax, plus 20% Austrian VAT).
 Business-to-Business (B2B) orders made by business customers (including Amazon Business customers) with a valid Austrian or EU VAT Registration Number (VRN) are exempt from the tax.
 Note : For recurring Subscribe & Save deliveries, nothing changes for the customer at the moment and subscriptions continue as usual.
 How customers will see the tax
 The tax will appear on the product detail page when the shipping address is set to Austria, and as a distinct line item at checkout and order confirmation. It is not merged with the product subtotal, delivery charges, or any other fee. A standalone tax receipt is issued for every eligible orders, separate to the product invoice.
 How the tax will affect your prices
 Your listed product price does not change. The tax is collected from customers at checkout as a separate charge. It doesn’t affect your pricing or selling fees.
 Refunds and cancellations
 If the order is cancelled before any parcel is dispatched, or all items in the order are returned, the €2.40 tax (including VAT) is refunded to customers. If at least one item is retained after the order is delivered, the tax is non-refundable.

 Hola:
Con entrada en vigor el 31 de octubre de 2026, se asignarán algunos de tus ASIN en nuestras tiendas europeas a categorías de tarifas actualizadas.
Las categorías de tarifas describen qué tipo de producto es un ASIN y pueden ser diferentes de la categoría en la que aparece el ASIN en nuestras tiendas. Cada ASIN de nuestro catálogo sólo puede pertenecer a una única categoría de tarifas. De forma periódica, revisamos los ASIN para asegurarnos de que tengan asignadas las categorías de tarifas correctas, tal y como se muestra en nuestras directrices de las categorías de tarifas .

 You’ve been enrolled in EPR Pay on Behalf for Amazon.co.uk
 Hello,
 You've been automatically enrolled in the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Pay on Behalf service for your sales of Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) and Packaging on Amazon.co.uk.
 Check my subscription
 What is Extended Producer Responsibility?
 EPR is a set of environmental laws that places responsibility for a product’s life cycle, including end-of-life waste management, on the companies that first place those products on the market. These companies are typically referred to as ‘producers’.
 What is EPR Pay on Behalf?
 EPR Pay on Behalf helps you meet your EPR reporting and eco-contribution fee obligations for sales in Amazon’s stores and reduces the risk of disruption to your selling privileges. Learn more .
 Why have I been enrolled in EPR Pay on Behalf?
 You were automatically enrolled as you met all the criteria below:
 You were considered a Producer under the UK Environment Code.
 You sold at least one product subject to EPR obligations on Amazon.co.uk.
 Your place of establishment is outside of the United Kingdom.
 What will I be charged?
 Service fee: £10 per half year for Packaging and £5 per quarter for Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE), charged within thirty days of your enrollment Eco-contribution fees: Variable based on your sales volume, held in reserve each month and charged after the reporting period ends.
 Note: You'll be charged £55 in service fees for sales periods from 2025 through the current period, by October 31 2026. This is the sum of the standard service fees above for each applicable period.
 Service fees and eco-contribution fees are charged and invoiced separately. For more information, go to EPR Pay on Behalf fees, account level reserves and refunds .
 Where can I see which of my products are classified under Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) and Packaging?
 You can check your product classifications in the EPR Category Report:
 Go to Amazon Fulfilment Reports in Seller Central
 In the left navigation bar, find the EPR section
 Click EPR Category Reports
 Choose the reporting year and period you'd like to review
 Download your report in either .csv or .txt format
 Filter for Amazon.co.uk in the “Amazon_Marketplace” column, followed by "Primary Packaging" for Packaging and "EEE" for WEEE in the “EPR_Category” column
 The report shows how your products have been classified based on your listing information on Amazon.co.uk, including which items fall under the applicable category. Reports for the previous month become available after the 20th day of the current month.
 How can I unsubscribe?
 Established outside the UK: Stop selling goods subject to Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) and Packaging EPR obligations on Amazon.co.uk. You'll still be charged for sales made before you remove your listings.
 Established in the UK: Submit proof of your UK business address via Selling Partner Support . Service fees already charged will be refunded after unenrollment.
 Go to EPR Pay on Behalf in the United Kingdom to find out more about EPR categories, eco-contribution fees, reporting cycles and service costs.

96
 For security, set up passkey login to maintain account access
 Hello,
 Starting in two weeks, passkeys will start to be required on a rolling basis for Amazon accounts. This will be required for all of your accounts, including Seller Central and Amazon.com . As part of our ongoing commitment to security, we're increasing passkey usage to all accounts to protect against unauthorized access and fraud.
 Passkeys are a secure, passwordless way to sign in using your device's built-in authentication—like fingerprint, face recognition, or PIN. They can't be phished or stolen, and they're supported by most modern smartphones, tablets, and operating systems.
 Set up your passkey, as it will be required for every login after that date. If you haven’t set one up yet, you’ll be prompted to enroll. Your password will remain on file as a backup recovery option but won’t be available for logging in.
 We recommend setting up passkeys on at least two devices in case a device is unavailable. Passkeys sync automatically across devices signed into the same Apple ID, Google account, or Microsoft account.
 To set up a passkey:
- Log in to Seller Central .
- Go to Login & Security .
- Select Set up beside Passkeys .
- Follow the on-screen instructions to complete set up (takes less than two minutes). Users with shared Amazon accounts must register any additional people accessing the account as secondary users to create their own passkey and log in separately.
 To add secondary users:
- Go to Settings and select User Permissions .
- Select the desired account for the new user.
- Enter the user’s contact information and select Send invitation . The secondary user will need a brand-new email address that has not been used on any Amazon account before.
- Repeat for all new users that need to be added.
- Request new users to follow the email instructions. Note : Only users who have registered as secondary users will be able to set up a passkey and log in separately to the shared account. Once registered, secondary users can log in and create a passkey.
 For issues setting up or using your passkey, our support team will respond in under 24 hours at Get help and resources . If you can't set up a passkey due to device or technical issues, contact Seller Support immediately.
 If you lose access to your passkey, you can contact [Seller Support] to verify your identity and quickly regain access.
 For instructions on how to set up secondary users, go to Passkey verification .
 For more information, go to About Passkey and Use Passkey on Multiple Devices . For passkey video walkthroughs, go to our Passkey YouTube playlist .

 CSBA Insights Dashboard
 Get the most out of Customer Service by Amazon
 Use the CSBA Insights dashboard in Seller Central to:
- Review customer service contacts handled by Amazon
- Find ways to improve customer experience
- Reduce contact and return rates
 Follow these practices to prevent customer confusion and minimize your workload:
- Monitor the Response Needed inbox within the Buyer-Seller Messaging Service . In the rare case that we need your help to resolve a customer issue, we'll summarize the conversation and pass the contact to you. You're expected to answer within 24 hours to ensure a great customer experience. You’ll still be responsible for pre-order inquiries.
- Avoid initiating 1:1 contact with customers. If you reach out to customers directly, Amazon can no longer support the customer regarding that order and you'll have to take responsibility for the rest of the conversation.
- Provide valid tracking. Include a valid tracking number with every shipment. This is the best way to prevent customers from contacting customer service.
- Improve product descriptions based on refunds. More accurate product descriptions can help manage customer expectations.
- Was a customer issued a refund incorrectly? If Amazon issues a refund and you don't think that you should be held financially responsible, do not contact the customer. Instead, file a claim for reimbursement via Seller Assurance for E-Commerce Transactions (SAFE-T). Learn more about SAFE-T claim eligibility and filing processes .
 CSBA Insights Dashboard
 How are CSBA fees calculated and applied?
 Fees are applied automatically to every shipped unit that is fulfilled by the merchant throughout Q4-2026. To learn more about program fees, go to
 Customer Service by Amazon fees .
- CSBA fees are not applied to any FBA, Easy Ship, or seller-fulfilled Prime units
- CPU rate is only calculated based on post-order contacts that Amazon handles on your behalf
- In rare instances, the contact count used for fee calculations may be lower than the total count shown on your dashboard. The difference in contacts counts does not impact your fees.
 For additional guidance, go to the
 CSBA help page .
